title: Retrenchment among Employees Aged 63 and Older in Last Five Years
what_it_is: Retrenchment among Employees Aged 63 and Older in Last Five Years

sections.label: Retrenchment rates for older residents
sections.summary: From 2018 to 2022, retrenchment incidence for residents aged 63 and over averaged 3.8 per 1,000, below the overall 6.1, with about 450 retrenched yearly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: From 2018 to 2022, the average incidence of retrenchment among residents aged 63 and over was 3.8 per 1,000 resident employees, lower than the overall figure of 6.1 for the entire resident workforce.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Over the same period, the absolute number of retrenched residents aged 63 and over remained low, at an average of 450 per year.

sections.label: EAP quantum versus retrenchment benefits
sections.summary: The EAP quantum is tied to the legal re-employment obligation and should not be compared to retrenchment benefits, which are not mandated by law and vary across companies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The EAP quantum is tied to the legal obligation to offer re-employment and should not be compared to retrenchment benefits, which are not mandated by law.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The quantum of retrenchment benefit is usually stipulated in the employment contract or is negotiated in a collective agreement between unions and companies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: It thus varies across companies, though the vast majority of employers do follow the Tripartite Advisory on Managing Excess Manpower and Responsible Retrenchment in paying retrenchment benefits, generally paying between two weeks and one month of salary per year of service, to eligible employees.

sections.label: EAP purpose and calibration
sections.summary: The EAP should not be compared to retrenchment benefits because it helps those not re-employed tide over until they find other re-employment opportunities, and its quantum is carefully calibrated.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, it is not the other way around.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: And the EAP should not be compared to retrenchment benefits, because it is meant to help those who are not re-employed, to tide them over a period of time until they find other re-employment opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The EAP quantum recommended in the tripartite guidelines on the re-employment of older employees, as I said, is carefully calibrated.

sections.label: Cheaper retrenchment benefit incentive
sections.summary: If paying retrenchment benefits is cheaper than paying EAP, it may become a perverse incentive to retrench a worker before retirement age.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: If the cost of paying retrenchment benefits is cheaper than paying EAP, it may well be that it will become a perverse incentive to retrench a worker before retirement age instead.

sections.label: Retrenchment benefits beyond age 63
sections.summary: The question asks whether retrenchment benefits are extended to workers beyond age 63 but before the end of their re-employment retirement age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: Then, perhaps the question that I should ask is: is the Senior Minister of State aware of whether retrenchment benefits are extended to workers beyond the age of 63, but before they reach the end of their re-employment retirement age?

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: I suppose for employers who really want to take care of their employees, there is no real reason why he or she cannot extend benefits to employees beyond the retirement age.
